div.head: VIII Atr 19
div.ab: Gif man mæssepreost tihtlige, þe regollice libbe, andfealdre spræce, mæssige, gif he durre, ⁊ ladige hine on ðam husle silf hine silfne;
Gif man mæssepreost tihtlige þe regollice libbe andfealdre spræce, mæssige, gif he durre, ⁊ ladige hine on ðam husle silf hine silfne.
Gif man mæssepreost tihtlige, þe regollice libbe, andfealdre spræce, mæssige, gif he durre, and ladige hine on ðam husle silf hine silfne.
Wenn ein Priester, der kanonisch lebt, mit einfacher Anklage bezichtigt wird, so lese er, wenn er es wagt, Messe und reinige allein sich selbst durch den Abendmahlsgenuss.
If a priest who lives according to the rule is charged with a simple accusation, let him say mass, if he dares, and clear himself alone by [taking] the sacrament.
If a simple accusation is brought against a priest who lives according to a rule, he shall say mass, if he dares, and by his own asseveration clear himself by the Holy Communion.
And if a mass-priest, who lives according to a rule, is charged with a simple accusation, he is to say mass, if he dares, and alone clear himself on the host itself;
If a simple accusation is brought against a priest who lives according to a rule, he shall celebrate the Mass if he dares, and exculpate himself on his own through the sacrament.

note.quote: It contains VIII Ethelred, 1.1–5.1, on sanctuary, and 19–27.1, on accusations against men in orders

div.note: D's ‘andfealdre’ is so in 19 and 20; compare I Cn 5, 5.1.; AZ: corrected against Rabin p. 196 / 197, October 2026 (was “∅”, now “|”)
simple accusation: That is, an accusation against which the accused requires only the oath of a single supporting witness.
on his own through the sacrament: In effect, the celebration of the Mass here substitutes for the oath of exculpatory witness.

note.seg: Das Stück 19—27, 1 wiederholt I Cn 5—5, 4 = Hn 64, 8. Vgl. Gl Geistliche 19ff. 28b, wonach als Eideshelfer auch hier zunächst Genossen (s. d. Gl 3b) der geistlichen Gilde anzunehmen sind; s. u. 24. 27. In Canterbury 30 mansuras tenent clerici de villa in gildam suam unter dem Erzbischof vór 1066; Domesday I 3. Auch am Yorker Dom bestand solcher geferscipe; Northu 2, 1. 45.—Zur Form andfeald vgl. Wb S. 45: d 1; Sievers Gram. § 198

The section 19—27, 1 is repeated in I Cn 5—5, 4 = Hn 64, 8. Cf. Gl Geistliche 19ff. 28b, according to which the oath-helpers here too are to be taken as being in the first place fellow members (see that word in Gl 3b) of the clerical gild; see below 24. 27. In Canterbury 30 mansuras tenent clerici de villa in gildam suam under the archbishop before 1066; Domesday I 3. Such a geferscipe also existed at York Minster; Northu 2, 1. 45.—On the form andfeald cf. Wb p. 45: d 1; Sievers Gram. § 198
Vgl. Gl Abendmahlsprobe 1f. 6, worüber Dahn Bausteine II 18. 47; Brunner II 413 und (gegen Hilse Gottesurteil der Abendmahlsp. 27) Kaegi Urspr. der Ordalien Anm. 75
Cf. Gl Abendmahlsprobe 1f. 6, on which see Dahn Bausteine II 18. 47; Brunner II 413 and (against Hilse Gottesurteil der Abendmahlsp. 27) Kaegi Urspr. der Ordalien note 75
This section from cap. 19–cap. 27 is repeated in I Cn. 5–5, 4; cf. Wi. 16–19.

i.e. by taking part in the communion service. The administration of the sacrament in this case takes the place of an oath of purgation, see Liebermann, ii. p. 263, s.v. Abendmahlsprobe, 6; Brunner, ii. p. 413⁷⁴; Dahr, Bausteine, ii. 18; Lea, Superstition and Force, pp. 304–11.
